basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 4.' and it opens 'Vers. 4. Faciamus nobis turrim. Timebant ne iterum fieret diluvium, et ideo auctore'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 4. Faciamus nobis turrim. Timebant ne iterum fieret diluvium, et ideo auctore Nemrod voluerunt turrim facere altissimam in qua, si diluvium | iterum fieret, salvarentur. Bitumen enim aquis dissolvi non poterat. Nulla enim re dissolvi potest, postquam siccatum fuerit nisi menstruo sanguine.
